clue.text: Person economising over a couple of pages, recyclable stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over and covers the other, so the first is wrapped round the second

parts.note: someone who scrapes by, saving every penny, is a scraper
the letter A with two P abbreviations for page around it

explanation.surface: A thrifty person sorting through a few pages of material fit for the recycling bin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means covering, so the person economising wraps round the A and two Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper already used on one side and kept for jotting or recycling is waste material, hence recyclable stuff.

clue.text: Indian, in prison, upset, irate, maltreated

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: jug is slang for a prison

indicators.note: the letters of the word are treated roughly and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry Indian in jail complains of rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns JUG into GUJ; 'maltreated' turns IRATE into ERATI. GUJERATI is a variant spelling of Gujarati.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gujerati is a person from the state of Gujarat in western India, so a native of that country.

clue.text: Theatric saga I composed, ending of which is kept secret

definitions.text: Theatric saga I composed, ending of which is kept secret

indicators.note: to compose is to put together in an arrangement, so the letters are set in a new order
only the final letter of the word which is taken

explanation.surface: A writer boasts of a dramatic saga whose conclusion nobody is allowed to reveal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges THEATRICSAGAI plus H (the last letter of 'which', from 'ending of'). As a whole, the clue describes the author of The Mousetrap, whose audiences are asked to keep the ending to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime novelist wrote the play The Mousetrap, whose twist ending theatregoers are famously sworn not to reveal.

clue.text: Dramatist arranging central part for top actor

indicators.note: the answer is a run taken from the middle of the two words, spanning where they meet

explanation.surface: A playwright reshuffling the middle section to suit a leading performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatist' and 'arranging' look like an anagram, but the letters sit in order across dramatiST ARranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading performer in a cast, the biggest name on the bill, is its headline celebrity.

clue.text: Female guardians he is with for each day of each month

parts.note: contracted, he is becomes he's
per is Latin for for each, as in per head
in the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 13th or 15th of every month

explanation.surface: Women keeping watch on a man who visits daily throughout the month.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these nymphs guarded the tree of golden apples in a garden at the world's western edge.

clue.text: In a way disturbed or hurt an athlete

indicators.note: the word In says one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: manner means a way of doing something

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: A sportsman was somehow upset or injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'athlete' at the end looks like part of the fodder, but it is the definition; only 'or hurt an' is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance competitor in a race of about 26 miles is a kind of sportsman.

clue.text: See 6
Location of cathedral, south of river bank

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece south of another is written below it

parts.note: Ely is a small city in Cambridgeshire famous for its cathedral

explanation.surface: Directions to a cathedral city lying below a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverside noun, but it is a verb: to bank on someone is to depend on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to count on it, the same as depending on it.

clue.text: Strongly advise dividing bed and finally plant one vegetable

indicators.note: one piece splits the other by sitting inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
to urge is to advise strongly

indicators.note: only the last letter of each of the next two words is taken

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: break up the bed and finally put in a single plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' governs both 'plant' and 'one', giving two letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette is a small marrow eaten as a vegetable, called zucchini in North America.

clue.text: Entertain one victim of 25, nonetheless

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: read as none-less, the word asks for an O, the letter that looks like zero or none, to be removed

parts.note: a mouse is what a mousetrap, the answer to 25, catches

explanation.surface: Even so, a mouse caught in a trap may still provide some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' looks like a link meaning 'even so', but read as 'O-less' it drops the O from MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to keep them entertained and make them laugh.

clue.text: Assistant has something to drink — not drinking inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a beer is something to drink
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A helper is offered a drink but turns it down, being on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts TT within A BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter is someone who helps or encourages another, usually in wrongdoing, so an assistant.

clue.text: Present line in 21 down, say, without elaboration

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: Hamlet, the answer to 21 down, is an example of a play
someone present is in

explanation.surface: An actor delivers a line from Hamlet simply.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is HAMLET, a play; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something simply, with no frills or embellishment, is speaking without elaboration.

clue.text: Drama, mostly including extreme characters, in open area of city

indicators.note: including says one piece holds the other inside it
most but not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a play is a drama
A and Z are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A theatrical performance, mostly featuring eccentrics, takes place in a city square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme characters' sounds like eccentric people, but it means the letters at the alphabet's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square or open space in a town, often Spanish in origin.

clue.text: Female protester has changed character in this prison

indicators.note: one letter of the name is swapped for another

parts.note: Emmeline Pankhurst led the British suffragettes campaigning for votes for women

explanation.surface: A suffragette undergoes a change of personality while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the N in PANKHURST to R. Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight; Pankhurst was jailed many times, which suits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkhurst is a well-known British high-security jail on the Isle of Wight, so the prison the clue points to.

clue.text: Power an emperor abused, eg Nero or Caligula

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: abused letters are mistreated and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler misused his power, as Nero or Caligula did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' turns AN EMPEROR into ROPERNAME, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero and Caligula are names of particular people, examples of a noun naming one individual.

clue.text: Assumes a certain form and speaks with heat, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall into a poor new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a particular appearance and speaks hotly, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges SPEAKS and HEAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: When something gradually develops a definite form or outline, it is said to be forming up in that way.

clue.text: Unusually kind performance in 21 down

definitions.note: a figure appearing in the play Hamlet

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remarkably gracious turn on stage in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges KIND PERFORMANCE. The play's title role is Hamlet, the Danish heir.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Shakespeare's tragedy is the heir to the Danish throne, a role in that play.

clue.text: See 3
Politician supporting German company re hearing

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP backs a German car firm at a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory means relating to the sense of hearing, as in the auditory nerve.

clue.text: Makes new arrangement, adding note for these instruments

indicators.note: adding the letter puts it into the other word

parts.note: to reorder is to arrange afresh
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musician rearranges a score, adding a note for the woodwind section.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorders are simple wooden or plastic wind instruments played by blowing into a mouthpiece.

clue.text: 25, perhaps, may be said to make one smile

definitions.meaning: bait put in a mousetrap, the answer to 25

definitions.text: may be said to make one smile
definitions.meaning: the word photographers ask people to say so they look cheerful

explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally bait for mice, and the word a photographer asks you to say for a grin.

clue.text: Entertained everyone sitting initially in the pit

parts.note: to have guests round is to entertain them, so had means entertained

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the next two words is used

explanation.surface: Theatre: the whole audience was seated at first in the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pit' suggests a theatre's stalls, but here it is the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hades is the underworld, and the pit is an old name for hell.

clue.text: Person acting badly allowed in village

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A poor actor is permitted to stay in a small rural community.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small settlement, smaller than a village and usually without a church.

clue.text: Among schemers, one poet who extolled appeal of 11 25?

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the words that follow, across their join

explanation.surface: Among a group of plotters, one writer praised the lure of an improved trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 25 is 'a better mousetrap': Ralph Waldo Emerson is credited with saying the world will beat a path to the door of whoever builds one.
explanation.definitionFit: The American essayist and poet is credited with the saying that the world will beat a path to an inventor's door.

clue.text: Part for gifted amateur that's found in 25, perhaps

indicators.note: part says just a piece of the following words, across their join, is wanted

explanation.surface: A role for a talented non-professional actor in a famous play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a stage role; it asks for a piece of giftED AMateur.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cheese of the kind traditionally put in a mousetrap as bait.

clue.text: Right English striker for another game

parts.note: a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A right-footed English forward lines up for a second fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, another game.

clue.text: King exposed, hence disorderly flight

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
a secret that is out has been exposed

explanation.surface: With the king's cover blown, his supporters scatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a defeat in which the beaten side runs off in confusion.

clue.text: Musician's very limited attack

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A performer's rather half-hearted assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims ASSAIL to ASSAI. In musical directions, as in 'allegro assai', it means very.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is the Italian term in musical directions meaning extremely, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: 6 7 and drama staged by 21 down

definitions.meaning: a long runner: the London play that has been running continuously since 1952
the play within the play that the Danish prince has performed to catch his uncle

explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's record-breaking London play shares its title with the name Hamlet gives the play he stages.
